root_cause.text: `dtv5100_i2c_msg()` in the `drivers/media/usb/dvb-usb/dtv5100.c` DVB-USB driver failed to validate the user-controlled `rlen` before using it to `memcpy()` into the fixed-size `st->data` buffer, allowing an out-of-bounds write/read when `rlen` exceeded `sizeof(st->data)`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (rlen > sizeof(st->data)) { warn("rlen = %x is too big!\n", rlen); return -EINVAL; }` immediately before `memcpy(st->data, rbuf, rlen);`, and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state that `rlen` is user-controlled and that values larger than `sizeof(st->data)` trigger an out-of-bounds condition.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a length guard to prevent copying more I2C data than the destination buffer can hold.
intent_record.what: A bounds check was added before memcpy in dtv5100_i2c_msg: if rlen is larger than sizeof(st->data), the function now logs a warning and returns -EINVAL instead of copying the data.
intent_record.how: This prevents an oversized read length from overflowing st->data, avoiding memory corruption and rejecting invalid I2C transfer sizes at runtime.

relevance_review.reason: The change adds a length check before copying I2C data into a fixed-size buffer, which directly matches the root cause of missing validation of user-controlled rlen before memcpy() in dtv5100_i2c_msg().
